neighbours.label: the end piece of the surname of a 19th-century English-language poet (Longf|ellow, Words|worth, Whitt|ier)
fire: Our teacher read a long poem by Henry Longfellow aloud.
William Wordsworth walked for miles around the lakes.
John Greenleaf Whittier wrote against slavery in New England.
She keeps a worn copy of Longfellow on the shelf.
Many schoolchildren once learned Wordsworth by heart.
A statue of Longfellow stands in the middle of Portland.
The anthology opens with Whittier and then Wordsworth.
Fans of Longfellow gathered at his old house in Cambridge.
quiet: Our teacher read a long story by Henry James aloud.
William Harris walked for miles around the lakes.
John Greene wrote against slavery in New England.
She keeps a worn copy of Dickens on the shelf.
Many schoolchildren once learned Latin by heart.
A statue of Lincoln stands in the middle of Portland.
The anthology opens with Hardy and then Austen.
Fans of Baseball gathered at the old park in Cambridge.
